subject: physics
title: Work done and energy transfer
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Work done and energy transfer — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.5.2.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Work done and energy transfer, specification section 4.5.2.
final_note: You worked through Work done and energy transfer — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: When a force causes an object to move through a distance, work is done on the object. A force does work on an object when the force causes a displacement of the object; a force that causes no displacement does no work, however large it is or however long it is applied.

The movement of the object caused by the force. Work is done only when the force produces a displacement, so both a force and a movement are needed. If the object does not move, there is no displacement and no work is done by that force.

concepts.term: Distance moved along the line of action of the force
concepts.def: The distance used in the work done equation is the distance the object moves along the line of action of the force, that is, the distance moved in the direction in which the force acts. Movement at right angles to a force is not distance along its line of action, so that force does no work.

The work done by a force on an object can be calculated using: work done = force × distance (moved along the line of action of the force), written in symbols as W = F s. This equation is not given on the exam equation sheet, so it must be recalled and applied.

concepts.term: Symbols and units in W = F s
concepts.def: In W = F s: work done, W, in joules, J; force, F, in newtons, N; distance, s, in metres, m. The distance must be in metres before it is substituted, so a distance given in centimetres or kilometres has to be converted first.

The joule, J, is the unit of work done. One joule of work is done when a force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre. So a 1 N force moving an object 2 m along its line of action does 2 J of work.

Multiplying newtons by metres gives newton-metres, and 1 joule = 1 newton-metre. The two units are identical in size, so converting between them changes only the name and never the number: 350 N m of work is 350 J of work.

Doing work is one way of transferring energy. The work done by a force on an object, in joules, is the energy transferred by that force, in joules. Work done and energy transferred are therefore the same quantity measured in the same unit.

concepts.term: Describing the energy transfer when work is done
concepts.def: Describe the transfer by naming the store energy comes from and the store it goes to. Lifting a box steadily: chemical store of the person to the gravitational potential store of the box. Pushing a trolley to speed it up: chemical store of the person to the kinetic store of the trolley. Braking a car: kinetic store of the car to thermal store of the brakes.

Work done against the frictional forces acting on an object causes a rise in the temperature of the object. Dragging a crate across a rough floor, or braking a bicycle, transfers energy to thermal stores, so the surfaces that rub together become warmer.

mcqs.q: In which of these situations is work done on the object by the force described?
options: A sledge is pulled forwards and slides 4 m along the ground
A shopper stands still holding a heavy bag for a minute
A waiter walks 5 m holding a loaded tray level in one hand
A driver pushes a stalled van hard but it will not budge
mcqs.explain: The pulling force causes a displacement of the sledge along its own line of action, so work is done on the sledge.

mcqs.q: A student holds a box weighing 40 N at a constant height for 15 s. How much work does the student's upward force do on the box?
options: 0 J
mcqs.explain: The box has no displacement, so s = 0 and W = 40 × 0 = 0 J.

mcqs.q: A cyclist pushes a broken bike with a steady force of 25 N along the line of action of the force, moving it 80 m. What is the work done on the bike?
Which symbol equation matches 'work done = force × distance (moved along the line of action of the force)'?
options: W = F / s
W = F s
F = W s
s = W F
mcqs.explain: Work done, W, is the force, F, multiplied by the distance, s, moved along its line of action.

mcqs.q: In the equation W = F s, which units belong with each quantity?
options: W in newtons, F in joules, s in metres
W in joules, F in newtons, s in metres
W in joules, F in newtons, s in centimetres
W in watts, F in newtons, s in metres
mcqs.explain: This is exactly the specification's list: work done in J, force in N, distance in m.

mcqs.q: One joule of work is done in which of these situations?
options: A force of one newton acts on an object for one second
A force of one newton moves an object 1 m sideways
A force of one newton is applied but nothing moves
A force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition of one joule of work done.

mcqs.q: A machine does 4500 N m of work. What is this work done in joules?
mcqs.explain: 1 joule = 1 newton-metre, so the number is unchanged and only the unit's name differs.

mcqs.q: Which statement about newton-metres and joules is correct?
options: 1 newton-metre of work is equal to 1000 joules of work
The newton-metre measures force, the joule measures work
The newton-metre measures work, the joule measures heat
1 newton-metre of work is exactly equal to 1 joule of work
mcqs.explain: The specification states 1 joule = 1 newton-metre, so the two units are identical in size.

mcqs.q: A student lifts a box steadily from the floor onto a shelf. Which best describes the energy transfer as work is done on the box?
options: Chemical store of the student to the kinetic store of the box as it rises
Gravitational potential store of the box to chemical store of the student
Chemical store of the student to gravitational potential store of the box
Chemical store of the student is used up and is not transferred anywhere
mcqs.explain: The lifting force causes an upward displacement, and the box ends up higher, so its gravitational potential store fills.

mcqs.q: A car brakes and comes to rest. Work is done against the frictional forces at the brakes. Which best describes what happens?
options: The kinetic store of the car empties and the energy is destroyed
The kinetic store of the car empties and the brakes rise in temperature
The kinetic store empties and the brakes stay at the same temperature
The thermal store of the brakes empties into the car's kinetic store
mcqs.explain: Work done against friction transfers energy to thermal stores, so the temperature of the brakes rises.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of work being done against the frictional forces acting on an object?
options: The energy of the object is destroyed
The object slows but does not warm
The temperature of the object falls
The temperature of the object rises
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification states happens when work is done against friction.

mcqs.q: A cyclist brakes for a long time going downhill and the brake blocks become hot. Why?
options: Friction destroys the bike's energy and heat is what is left over
The blocks gain energy in their kinetic store and so become hot
The rider squeezes the levers hard, and squeezing hard makes heat
Work is done against friction, so the blocks rise in temperature
mcqs.explain: The blocks rub on the moving wheel, and work done against those frictional forces raises their temperature.

mcqs.q: A porter carries a 60 N suitcase 20 m along a level corridor, keeping it at a constant height. How much work does the upward supporting force do on the suitcase?
options: 3 J
0 J
mcqs.explain: The suitcase moves horizontally, so the distance moved along the line of action of the upward force is zero.

mcqs.q: A box is dragged 5 m by a steady 30 N force. It is then dragged 10 m by the same 30 N force. How does the work done compare?
options: It stays the same, because the same size of force is used on both journeys
It quadruples, because the force and the distance have both been doubled
It doubles, because work done is force × distance and the distance doubles
It halves, because the same force is now spread over a longer distance
mcqs.explain: W = F s with F unchanged and s doubled from 5 m to 10 m, so 150 J becomes 300 J.

mcqs.q: A force of 12 N pushes a book 50 cm across a desk along the line of action of the force. What is the work done on the book?
options: 6 J

mcqs.q: A cleaner pushes a trolley at a steady speed across a rough floor with a force of 25 N for 8 m, doing 200 J of work. What happens to that 200 J?
options: It is transferred to thermal stores, so the trolley rises in temperature
It is transferred to the kinetic store, so the trolley gets faster and faster
It is used up in overcoming friction, so that energy no longer exists
It is transferred to the gravitational potential store of the trolley
mcqs.explain: The speed is steady, so the work is done against friction, and that raises the temperature of the object.

specSource: AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification; section 4.5.2 Work done and energy transfer
